summary.tagline: A woodland journey to the cascading waters of Gwydir Forest.

travel.headline: Visit the Famous Waterfall from the Gwydir Forest
travel.reservation: Access to the waterfall trail via the Ty'n Llwyn car park does not currently require a formal entry reservation. Visitors should check the Natural Resources Wales website for the latest updates on forest access or local parking requirements before arrival.

days.title: Woodland Vistas and Waterfalls

stops.name: Swallow Falls
stops.detail: Follow the strenuous circular trail through woodland to reach a dedicated viewpoint overlooking the falls. The route features narrow paths and uneven surfaces, providing a natural perspective from the Gwydir side of the river.

days.driving: Allow 15 minutes for local transit; conditions vary based on forest road accessibility.
days.note: The 2.2-mile trail is strenuous with narrow paths; allow up to two and a half hours for a comfortable pace.

intel.title: Trail Surface Challenges
intel.text: The path consists of unmade and uneven surfaces including mud, rocks, and tree roots. Expect narrow sections less than 70 cm wide and several flights of steps.

intel.title: Ty'n Llwyn Facilities
intel.text: The Ty'n Llwyn car park serves as the primary trailhead and includes a wheelchair-accessible picnic table. Capacity information is not provided, so arrive early during peak seasons.

intel.title: Suggested Walking Time
intel.text: Official estimates suggest 1.5 to 2.5 hours to complete the Swallow Falls Trail loop. Factors like weather and trail mud may increase this duration.

intel.title: Local Supplies
intel.text: Fuel and supply availability at the trailhead is not documented in official sources. Visitors should verify services in nearby Betws-y-Coed before heading into the forest.

intel.title: Connectivity Status
intel.text: Specific mobile signal strength for the Gwydir Forest area is not cited. It is recommended to download maps before departing as forest canopy may impact reception.

plan.arrival: Collect a vehicle in Betws-y-Coed and proceed to the Ty'n Llwyn car park. Use the accessible picnic area for a pre-hike briefing.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are suitable for reaching regional car parks; check local road conditions for height or width restrictions.
plan.goldenHour: The waterfall viewpoint offers a resting bench suitable for late afternoon light, though deep woodland shadows will fall early.
